headline_marked: Govt imposes [[fresh austerity measures]] to curb inflation and spending
headline: Govt imposes fresh austerity measures to curb inflation and spending
summary: New restrictions halt the purchase of vehicles, construction of new buildings, and most government-funded foreign travel for the 2026-27 fiscal year.
details: The government has introduced a new round of austerity measures for the 2026-27 fiscal year to rein in public expenditure, curb inflation, and preserve macroeconomic stability.
The Finance Division has directed all ministries, departments, autonomous bodies, and state-owned enterprises to cut costs from both operating and development budgets.
Spending on new motor vehicles, vessels, and aircraft has been suspended. Only electric vehicles may be purchased as replacements for cars older than 10 years, subject to approval.
The construction of new residential and non-residential government buildings is halted. Only projects that are at least 70% complete may continue with Finance Division approval.
Government-funded foreign training, seminars, and workshops have been suspended. However, travel for PhD/Master's scholarships or mandatory training remains permissible.
The move comes as the National Board of Revenue (NBR) faces a revenue shortfall of approximately Tk 88,000 crore for the 2025-26 financial year.
The economy is also struggling with high inflation, which averaged 8.68% in the 2025-26 fiscal year, alongside subdued private investment and global uncertainties.
caption:
No more new cars or foreign trips. The government is tightening its belt with strict new spending curbs.

The government has introduced a new round of austerity measures for the 2026-27 fiscal year to rein in public expenditure, curb inflation, and preserve macroeconomic stability.

The Finance Division has directed all ministries, departments, autonomous bodies, and state-owned enterprises to cut costs from both operating and development budgets.

Spending on new motor vehicles, vessels, and aircraft has been suspended. Only electric vehicles may be purchased as replacements for cars older than 10 years, subject to approval.

The construction of new residential and non-residential government buildings is halted. Only projects that are at least 70% complete may continue with Finance Division approval.

Government-funded foreign training, seminars, and workshops have been suspended. However, travel for PhD/Master's scholarships or mandatory training remains permissible.

The move comes as the National Board of Revenue (NBR) faces a revenue shortfall of approximately Tk 88,000 crore for the 2025-26 financial year.

The economy is also struggling with high inflation, which averaged 8.68% in the 2025-26 fiscal year, alongside subdued private investment and global uncertainties.
